payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, can the source-image paper and cup be identified, and is that paper visibly stuffed inside that cup?
node.criteria: Pass only if the edited image provides enough visual evidence to identify the same paper and cup shown in the source and shows the paper placed inside the cup with evidence it has been stuffed into it. Fail only if both objects are identifiable and the paper is visibly outside the cup or merely on its rim. Unknown if either object's identity, or their placement, cannot be established.
node.binding: Anchor “the paper” and “the cup” to the objects in the source image. Do not treat a visually different-looking item or object in the edited image as the same object without sufficient evidence.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows a white paper-like item and a blue cup, but the edited image shows a blue printed item and a reddish object. There is not enough visual evidence to identify these as the same paper and cup from the source or establish that the paper was stuffed inside the cup.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too vague and its evidence path is brittle: it names “the paper” and “the cup” without directing the checks to compare the source objects with the edited scene. The edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item in front of a reddish rounded object; neither is clearly identifiable as the source’s white paper and blue cup, and the item is not visibly stuffed inside a cup. But that visual mismatch alone does not establish that no requested progress occurred: the checks must assess whether any visible action or intermediate state advances stuffing the source paper into the source cup, while excluding unrelated edits. Clarify the binding and completion/progress criteria so the dependencies separately test visible completion and requested progress, and the parent returns no only when both are supported as absent; preserve unknown when object identity or progress cannot be determined. The high-confidence unresolved results are a reason to inspect whether the checks are overcautious or lack useful source-to-edit comparison guidance, not to force a label. There is no transport, schema, or dependency-execution failure indicated here.
s2: The node already states the key source-to-edit binding and correctly preserves unknown when identity or progress is unclear. The trace is a valid uncertainty, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure: the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a reddish rounded object, while the source shows white paper and a blue cup; the trace cannot reliably match either object or establish the requested action. Do not turn this mismatch into a no label or force a decision to match the reference. Improve the executable checks’ evidence path: explicitly compare candidate objects across source and edit using visible features, assess completion separately from intermediate progress, and count progress only when visible placement or action advances stuffing the matched source paper into the matched source cup. Keep unrelated edits out of the judgment, and retain unknown when identity or the relevant relation remains indeterminate. Inspect why the high-confidence uncertainty yields zero coverage—whether the checks lack useful comparison guidance or are appropriately cautious—without treating confidence or the reference label as atomic ground truth.
